Later payment of the annual licence fee, back fees and a late fee renews the credential going forward but does not reclassify shifts already worked
The trainee reaches 1500 hours or one year, whichever is shorter
The individual may no longer work as a pharmacy technician trainee unless one of the three stated exceptions applies

It does not by itself confer a pharmacy technician licence; the individual must still satisfy 247 CMR 8.02(3), and one who passed the limits before turning 18 must apply within 30 days of the 18th birthday

worked_examples.scenario: On her first shift a newly licensed pharmacy technician is told by a colleague that technicians may do only the handful of things 247 CMR 8.02(6) lists, so she declines to count tablets or enter prescriptions. Later the pharmacist, who is overseeing and directing her work, asks her to relay the pharmacist's offer to counsel to a waiting patient, and a second colleague asks her to telephone a prescriber to suggest a cheaper alternative drug and then to explain to the patient how to take the new medicine. Which of these tasks are hers?
steps: Fix the tier and the supervision. She holds a Board pharmacy technician licence, and 247 CMR 2.00 describes a pharmacy technician as performing pharmacy duties under the direct supervision of a pharmacist, which is what the overseeing and directing pharmacist is giving.

Test the colleague's reading. 247 CMR 8.02(6) sets a name-tag duty, two conditioned communications and a list of prohibited functions; it is not a list of the only tasks a technician may do, and 247 CMR 8.06(1)(b) expects the pharmacy to describe in writing the duties it delegates. Counting and prescription entry are delegable technical work.

Run the prohibited list. Suggesting an alternative drug to the prescriber is contact concerning therapy modification, and explaining how to take the medicine is patient counseling; 247 CMR 8.02(6)(d) closes both to a pharmacy technician whatever the pharmacist or a colleague is willing to allow.
Apply the express grant. 247 CMR 8.02(6)(b) lets a pharmacy technician relay to the patient the pharmacist's offer to counsel, and relaying the offer is not counseling.
worked_examples.resolution: She may count, enter prescriptions and relay the offer to counsel under the pharmacist's direct supervision, but may not call the prescriber about a therapy change or counsel the patient. The error the scenario invites runs in both directions: reading 247 CMR 8.02(6) as the whole of what a technician may do, and treating a willing colleague or pharmacist as able to open a function the regulation closes.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacy technician telephones a prescriber's office for authorization to refill a maintenance prescription. The pharmacist on duty had approved the technician making refill calls that morning. The prescriber's agent authorizes the refill but also raises the daily dose from one tablet to two. The technician asks whether she may write the change down and let the pharmacist verify it at the final check.
steps: Identify the authority the technician is working under. A pharmacy technician may request and accept refill authorizations under 247 CMR 8.02(6)(c) with the approval of the pharmacist on duty.
Read the condition attached to that authority. It applies only if no information has changed from the previous prescription, and the daily dose has changed.
Notice what the pharmacist's earlier approval covered. It was approval to make refill calls within the authority the regulation grants, not approval to accept information the authority excludes.

Check whether a later pharmacist check cures the problem. Final dispensing process validation is a separate function closed to technicians, and it is not a repair mechanism for a call that has already left technician scope.

Route the call. The pharmacy technician has no grant to receive changed or new prescription information: 247 CMR 9.04(8) gives receipt of new prescriptions over the telephone to the pharmacy intern and to the certified pharmacy technician with approval, the 247 CMR 8.02(6)(c) grant stops at unchanged refills, and carrying on the conversation about the new dose would be contact concerning therapy modification, which 247 CMR 8.02(6)(d) closes to technicians. The pharmacist takes the call.
worked_examples.resolution: The technician may not accept the dose change; the unchanged-information condition has failed and the pharmacist must handle the call. The error the scenario invites is treating pre-approval of refill calls as approval to accept whatever the call turns up, with the pharmacist's later verification imagined as a cure.

worked_examples.scenario: A Massachusetts pharmacy discovers that a staff member's certification from the certifying body lapsed a week ago. The individual's Board pharmacy technician licence is current. The shift is staffed with one pharmacist supporting four people, and this individual was one of the two certified pharmacy technicians on it. The manager assumes the only issue is a name tag.
steps: Separate the two credentials. The certifying body's certification and the Board pharmacy technician licence are different things, and only the certification has lapsed.

Apply the three consequences 247 CMR 8.04(3) attaches to that lapse: duties limited to those of a pharmacy technician under 247 CMR 8.02, use of the title pharmacy technician, and counting as a pharmacy technician in the supervisory ratios under 247 CMR 8.06(3).

Work out what the scope consequence removes. The individual can no longer receive new or omitted prescription information from a prescriber under the certified-technician authority, and can no longer perform a Schedule VI prescription transfer.
Work out what the ratio consequence does to the shift. The shift was built on two certified pharmacy technicians, and it now has one, so the staffing question is live rather than clerical.
Confirm what has not happened. The Board pharmacy technician licence is unaffected, so the individual continues to work, at the pharmacy technician tier.
worked_examples.resolution: The lapse changes scope, title and the supervisory-ratio arithmetic simultaneously, while leaving the Board licence intact. The error the scenario invites is treating the lapse as either a paperwork detail or as the end of the individual's ability to work, and missing the ratio consequence that actually disrupts the shift.

worked_examples.scenario: An applicant is 19, holds a high school diploma, is of good moral character and has no drug-related felony. He has just finished an in-house course his employer built, running 90 hours of classroom instruction and 150 hours on the bench, and the employer offers a signed letter attesting to his competence. He submits a licence application on the strength of the course and the letter.
steps: Confirm the four common requirements of 247 CMR 8.02(3). Age, education, good moral character and the absence of a drug-related felony conviction or admission to sufficient facts are all satisfied here.

Turn to the fifth requirement and remember it is a choice of three alternatives: certifying-body certification, a substantially equivalent out-of-state licence in good standing, or a Board-approved passing score on a Board-approved assessment examination.

Test the course against 247 CMR 8.02(4)(c). A Board-approved program of the generic kind needs a minimum of 120 hours of theoretical and 120 hours of practical instruction, and 90 hours of theory does not meet the minimum even though the two figures total 240.

Check content as well as hours. On the examination route 247 CMR 8.02(3)(e)3.a requires the Board-approved training program to cover job descriptions, pharmacy security, commonly used medical abbreviations, routes of administration, product selection, final check by pharmacists, guidelines for the use of pharmacy technicians, and any other Board requirements, so even a course that met both hour minimums would have to show that coverage.

Test the employer's letter. An attestation of general competence is not one of the three alternatives, and the only attestation the regulation provides for is the applicant's own attestation, under the pains and penalties of perjury and witnessed by the employer, of a minimum of 500 hours of employment as a pharmacy technician trainee.

Follow the training route to its end. Even a program that did qualify would not by itself license the applicant, because completing the program is the prerequisite to the Board-approved assessment examination rather than a substitute for it.
worked_examples.resolution: The application fails: the course does not meet the 120-hour theoretical minimum, the employer letter is not a recognised route, and no examination has been passed. The error the scenario invites is reading the hour requirement as a single 240-hour total and treating completion of training as the licence rather than as the gateway to the examination.

worked_examples.scenario: A 17-year-old pharmacy technician trainee has logged 1,620 hours over eleven months. During a staffing shortage the pharmacist in charge asks the trainee to answer the pharmacy telephone and take a new prescription from a prescriber's agent, offering to stand beside the trainee throughout the call.
steps: Take the employment limit first. The cap is 1500 hours or one year, whichever period is shorter, but the individual has not yet reached 18 years of age, and that is one of the three stated exceptions, so the trainee may still be working.

Note what the exception sets up rather than ends. An individual who worked beyond those limits before the 18th birthday shall submit an application for a pharmacy technician licence within 30 days of that birthday.

Turn to the telephone request. A pharmacy technician trainee may be authorized to perform the duties of a pharmacy technician, but only while acting under the direct supervision of a pharmacist and subject to the express exception in the same subsection.

Apply the exception. A pharmacy technician trainee may not take prescriptions over the telephone, and the pharmacist standing beside the trainee supplies the direct supervision the general grant already required rather than lifting the carve-out.
Separate the two questions in the answer. Continued employment is lawful under an exception to the hours limit; the telephone task is unlawful whatever the hours position.
worked_examples.resolution: The trainee may keep working under the age exception but may not take the prescription by telephone, and an application for a pharmacy technician licence is due within 30 days of the 18th birthday. The error the scenario invites is letting close supervision cure an express prohibition, and treating the hours exception as though it enlarged the trainee's duties.

worked_examples.scenario: In autumn 2026 a Massachusetts community pharmacy plans a clinic at which two licensed pharmacy technicians would give seasonal influenza vaccine to adults. One has completed an ACPE-approved practical immunization training program and holds a current basic CPR certificate; the other has neither. The manager points to the technician bar in 247 CMR and asks whether the clinic can run at all.
steps: Start with Massachusetts regulation. 247 CMR 8.02(6)(d) provides that a pharmacy technician may not administer medications or vaccines, and nothing in 247 CMR 8.00 relaxes that for a trained or supervised technician.

Then read the federal overlay. The PREP Act Declaration for COVID-19 countermeasures, as amended by its 12th Amendment, covers qualified pharmacy technicians who administer seasonal influenza vaccine to persons aged 19 and older according to CDC's/ACIP's standard immunization schedule through December 31, 2029, and states that State law that would otherwise prohibit them is preempted.

Test each technician against the Declaration's conditions: licensed or registered by the State board of pharmacy, acting under the supervision of a State-licensed pharmacist, an ACPE-approved practical training program, and a current basic CPR certificate. The trained technician can meet them; the untrained one cannot.
Build the supervision into the plan. The supervising pharmacist must be readily and immediately available to the immunizing technician, so the clinic cannot run with the pharmacist out of reach.
worked_examples.resolution: Under 247 CMR alone neither technician may vaccinate. Under the federal Declaration the trained technician is covered to give adult influenza vaccine on its conditions through December 31, 2029, and the untrained one is not. The error the scenario invites is treating either body of law as the whole answer: the Massachusetts bar is not a federal rule, and the federal coverage is neither unconditional nor permanent.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which tier may perform prescription transfers between pharmacies, and for which schedule?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Only a certified pharmacy technician, only for controlled substances in Schedule VI, and only with the approval of the pharmacist on duty.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A pharmacy technician trainee must be at least ______ years of age; a pharmacy technician must be at least ______ years of age.
An individual may not work as a pharmacy technician trainee for more than ______ hours or more than ______, whichever period is shorter.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 1500; one year. The three exceptions are a Board-granted extension, not yet having reached 18 years of age, and not yet having completed at least 500 trainee hours.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A generic Board-approved pharmacy technician training program must include a minimum of ______ hours of theoretical and ______ hours of practical instruction.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 120; 120. Both minimums must be met separately, not as a combined total.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: a Board-approved passing score on the assessment examination is, standing alone, one of the three eligibility alternatives.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. The examination route also requires successful completion of a Board-approved training program or a minimum of 500 hours of employment as a pharmacy technician trainee, attested under the pains and penalties of perjury and witnessed by the employer.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: When does a Massachusetts pharmacy technician licence expire, and what is the status of work done after that date?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Every two years on the birthdate of the licensee. Any practice as a pharmacy technician after the expiration date constitutes unlicensed practice and subjects the individual to the penalties established for unlicensed practice.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Name the three consequences that follow when a certified pharmacy technician's certification lapses.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Duties limited to those of a pharmacy technician under 247 CMR 8.02; use of the title pharmacy technician; and counting as a pharmacy technician in the 247 CMR 8.06(3) supervisory ratios.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: a pharmacy technician trainee may take a prescription over the telephone if the pharmacist supervising directly listens to the call.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. The prohibition is stated as an express exception to the grant of technician duties, so direct supervision does not lift it.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A pharmacy technician may request and accept refill authorizations with the pharmacist on duty's approval only if ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: no information has changed from the previous prescription.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which knowledge areas must a Board-approved pharmacy technician assessment examination cover?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Practice settings; the duties and responsibilities of a pharmacy technician in relationship to other pharmacy personnel; laws and regulations regarding the practice of pharmacy and patient confidentiality; medical abbreviations and symbols; common dosage calculations; and identification of drugs, dosages, routes of administration and storage requirements.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Under 247 CMR, name the functions closed to every technician tier however the pharmacy has written its protocols.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Administering medications or vaccines, performing drug utilization review, conducting clinical conflict resolution, contacting prescribers concerning therapy clarification or modification, providing patient counseling, and performing final dispensing process validation (247 CMR 8.02(6)(d) and 8.04(4)(e)). For vaccines federal law adds a separate layer: the PREP Act Declaration covers qualified pharmacy technicians giving COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccines on its conditions through December 31, 2029.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What must an individual do who worked beyond the trainee hours limits before turning 18?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Submit an application for a pharmacy technician licence within 30 days of the 18th birthday.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Does 247 CMR 8.00 list the routine technical tasks a pharmacy technician may perform?
retrieval_prompts.answer: No. 247 CMR 2.00 describes the technician as performing pharmacy duties under the direct supervision of a pharmacist, the pharmacy keeps a written description of the duties it delegates for production to the Board under 247 CMR 8.06(1)(b), and 247 CMR 8.00 bounds that delegation with a closed list of prohibited functions and with conditioned grants for particular communications and transfers.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: a licensed pharmacy technician, unlike a trainee, needs only general pharmacist supervision.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. 247 CMR 2.00 defines the pharmacy technician, like the trainee, as performing pharmacy duties under the direct supervision of a pharmacist, meaning a pharmacist who oversees and directs the technician's activities.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: May a certified pharmacy technician receive a new prescription over the telephone?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Yes, with the approval of the pharmacist on duty (247 CMR 9.04(8)); 247 CMR 8.04(4)(c) likewise lets the certified technician, after self-identification and with approval, receive new or omitted prescription information.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which topics must a Board-approved training program cover when it is the prerequisite to the assessment examination?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Job descriptions, pharmacy security, commonly used medical abbreviations, routes of administration, product selection, final check by pharmacists, guidelines for the use of pharmacy technicians, and any other requirements of the Board (247 CMR 8.02(3)(e)3.a).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What conditions does the federal PREP Act Declaration attach to a qualified pharmacy technician's vaccine administration, and when does that coverage end?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Supervision by a State-licensed pharmacist who is readily and immediately available; licensure or registration by the State board of pharmacy; an ACPE-approved practical training program; a current basic CPR certificate; FDA-authorized, approved or licensed vaccines given according to CDC's/ACIP's recommendations or standard immunization schedule; and compliance with the federal requirements for COVID-19 vaccine administration. For COVID-19 vaccines and seasonal influenza vaccines to persons aged three or older the coverage runs through December 31, 2029.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: an applicant's conviction arising from dispensing medication for reproductive health care always defeats the requirement of no drug-related felony conviction.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. Under 247 CMR 8.08 no person shall be denied initial licensure or renewal due to a conviction or other sanction arising from providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive or gender-affirming health care services, so long as the services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice there.

quick_review.text: Three tiers, three credentials: a trainee licence, a Board pharmacy technician licence, and that same licence plus a certifying body's certification.

A pharmacy technician applicant must be at least 18, a high school graduate or the equivalent or currently enrolled, of good moral character, and free of a drug-related felony conviction or admission to sufficient facts, and must then satisfy one of three alternatives; under 247 CMR 8.08 a sanction arising from reproductive or gender-affirming health care services that would have been lawful in Massachusetts and consistent with good professional practice there cannot be the reason initial licensure or renewal is denied.

The assessment-examination route is not standalone: it follows a Board-approved training program or a minimum of 500 hours of trainee employment attested under the pains and penalties of perjury and witnessed by the employer.

A generic Board-approved training program needs a minimum of 120 hours of theoretical and 120 hours of practical instruction; on-the-job training by a pharmacist runs on written pharmacy guidelines produced to the Board on request.

On the examination route the Board-approved training program must cover job descriptions, pharmacy security, commonly used medical abbreviations, routes of administration, product selection, final check by pharmacists, guidelines for the use of pharmacy technicians, and any other Board requirements.
The Board-approved examination covers six named knowledge areas, including laws and regulations on pharmacy practice and patient confidentiality, not calculations alone.
A pharmacy technician licence expires every two years on the licensee's birthdate, and practice after the expiration date is unlicensed practice.
Trainee employment is capped at 1500 hours or one year, whichever is shorter, with three exceptions, and a trainee may not take prescriptions over the telephone.

A pharmacy technician may relay the pharmacist's offer to counsel and, with the pharmacist on duty's approval, request and accept refill authorizations where nothing has changed from the previous prescription.

A certified pharmacy technician who self-identifies may, with the pharmacist on duty's approval, receive new or omitted prescription information and perform Schedule VI prescription transfers, and with that approval may receive new prescriptions over the telephone.

A lapsed certification limits the individual to pharmacy technician duties, the pharmacy technician title, and pharmacy technician counting in the supervisory ratios, while leaving the Board licence alone.

Technicians and trainees perform pharmacy duties under the direct supervision of a pharmacist. 247 CMR 8.00 does not list routine technical tasks; it closes six professional functions to every tier and attaches conditions to particular communications and transfers, and the pharmacist's judgmental functions may not be delegated.

Federal PREP Act coverage for qualified pharmacy technicians giving COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccines runs through December 31, 2029 on the Declaration's conditions and preempts contrary State law for those vaccines; it does not change 247 CMR.

decision_logic.condition: A task is proposed for a member of pharmacy technician staff.
decision_logic.action: Establish the tier from the credential actually held and confirm a pharmacist is giving direct supervision. Then ask three questions in order. Is the task one of the functions 247 CMR 8.02(6)(d) and 8.04(4)(e) close to every tier? If so, stop, whatever the pharmacist is willing to supervise. Is it a communication or transfer the regulations grant only to named tiers on conditions, such as refill authorizations, new or omitted prescription information, new prescriptions by telephone or Schedule VI transfers, or is it caught by the trainee's telephone bar? If so, apply that provision to this tier with its conditions. Otherwise, is it technical work the pharmacy has delegated? That work the individual may perform under direct supervision.

decision_logic.condition: The individual is a pharmacy technician trainee and the task is taking a prescription over the telephone.
decision_logic.action: Stop at the express carve-out. A trainee may not take prescriptions over the telephone, and direct supervision does not restore the authority. Where the call is only an unchanged refill authorization, note that the regulations do not settle whether the carve-out reaches it.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacy technician is asked to obtain a refill authorization.
decision_logic.action: Obtain the approval of the pharmacist on duty, then confirm that nothing has changed from the previous prescription; if anything has changed, hand the call to the pharmacist rather than recording the change for later verification.

decision_logic.condition: A certified pharmacy technician is asked to speak with a prescriber or to move a prescription to another pharmacy.
decision_logic.action: Have the individual identify him or herself as a certified pharmacy technician, obtain the pharmacist on duty's approval, and check the boundary: new or omitted prescription information, and new prescriptions by telephone, are permitted with that approval; therapy clarification or modification is not; and transfers reach Schedule VI only.

decision_logic.condition: A certification from the certifying body has lapsed.
decision_logic.action: Apply all three consequences together: reduce the individual to the 247 CMR 8.02 duties, change the title in use to pharmacy technician, and recalculate the supervisory ratio with the individual counted as a pharmacy technician. Leave the Board licence alone.

decision_logic.condition: A Board pharmacy technician licence has passed its expiration date.
decision_logic.action: Treat any further work as unlicensed practice and stop it. File the renewal application with the annual licence fee, back fees and late fee, and, where the lapse exceeds two years, expect the Board to determine other conditions before renewal.

decision_logic.condition: An applicant asks what still stands between a completed training program and a licence.
decision_logic.action: Check the program against the categories in 247 CMR 8.02(4), including the 120-hour theoretical and 120-hour practical minimums for a generic Board-approved program, and against the topics 247 CMR 8.02(3)(e)3.a requires it to cover, and then point to the Board-approved assessment examination that the training route exists to reach.

decision_logic.condition: A candidate is preparing for the Board-approved assessment examination.
decision_logic.action: Study all six named knowledge areas, treating law, regulation and patient confidentiality and the technician's duties in relationship to other pharmacy personnel as tested content alongside calculations.

decision_logic.condition: A question asks whether a Massachusetts pharmacy technician may administer a vaccine.
decision_logic.action: Answer in two layers. Under 247 CMR 8.02(6)(d) and 8.04(4)(e), no. Under the federal PREP Act Declaration, a qualified pharmacy technician is covered for COVID-19 vaccines and seasonal influenza vaccines to persons aged three or older through December 31, 2029 if every condition is met, and State law to the contrary is preempted for those vaccines; outside the countermeasures, ages, conditions and period it names, the Declaration gives the technician nothing.

decision_logic.condition: An applicant's record shows a conviction or other sanction.
decision_logic.action: Apply 247 CMR 8.02(3) or 8.03(2) as written, then ask whether the sanction arose from providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive or gender-affirming health care services that would have been lawful in Massachusetts and consistent with good professional practice there; if so, 247 CMR 8.08 bars denying initial licensure or renewal because of it.

ma_vs_federal.text: Massachusetts and federal law answer the technician vaccine question differently. 247 CMR 8.02(6)(d) and 8.04(4)(e) bar the pharmacy technician and the certified pharmacy technician from administering medications or vaccines, and nothing in 247 CMR 8.00 lifts that bar. The federal PREP Act Declaration for COVID-19 countermeasures, as amended by its 12th Amendment (89 FR 99875), covers qualified pharmacy technicians who administer FDA-authorized or FDA-licensed COVID-19 vaccines to persons aged three or older and seasonal influenza vaccines to persons aged three or older, and states that State law that would otherwise prohibit them from administering those vaccines is preempted.

The federal coverage is conditional. The technician must act under the supervision of a State-licensed pharmacist who is readily and immediately available, be licensed or registered by the State board of pharmacy, have completed an ACPE-approved practical training program in hands-on injection technique, clinical evaluation of indications and contraindications, and the recognition and treatment of emergency reactions, hold a current certificate in basic cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and give only FDA-authorized, approved or licensed vaccines according to CDC's/ACIP's recommendations or standard immunization schedule, complying with the CDC COVID-19 vaccination provider agreement and the other federal requirements for COVID-19 vaccine administration.

The federal coverage is also temporary and specific. Under section XII of the Declaration it runs through December 31, 2029 for technician-administered COVID-19 vaccines and seasonal influenza vaccines, the same Declaration covers COVID-19 tests and certain COVID-19 therapeutics on conditions of their own, and outside what it names the Declaration gives the technician nothing, so the 247 CMR bar stands.

exceptions.text: The trainee employment limit does not bite where the Board grants an extension, where the individual has not yet reached 18 years of age, or where the individual has not yet completed at least 500 hours of employment as a trainee. Employer staffing pressure is not among them.
The general grant of pharmacy technician duties to a trainee is expressly subject to the telephone carve-out, so the exception controls the grant rather than the reverse.
The pharmacy technician's refill authority under 247 CMR 8.02(6)(c) is unavailable as soon as any information has changed from the previous prescription.

The certified technician's prescription transfer authority extends only to controlled substances in Schedule VI, and the authority to receive prescription information yields where federal or state law otherwise prohibits it.

A licence lapsed for more than two years may attract other conditions determined by the Board as a prerequisite to renewal, so the ordinary fee-and-application route is not guaranteed to be the whole of it.

Under 247 CMR 8.08 no person shall be denied initial licensure or denied renewal due to any complaint, criminal charge, conviction, judgment, discipline, or other sanction due to providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, so long as the services provided would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice in Massachusetts. It qualifies the good moral character and drug-related felony requirements and the renewal rules alike.

timing_deadlines.event: Pharmacy technician licence term
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Expires every two years on the birthdate of the licensee
timing_deadlines.consequence: Any practice as a pharmacy technician after the expiration date constitutes unlicensed practice, subject to the penalties established for unlicensed practice.

timing_deadlines.event: Licence lapsed for more than two years
timing_deadlines.consequence: The Board may require other conditions it determines as a prerequisite to renewal, beyond the renewal application, annual fee, back fees and late fee.

timing_deadlines.event: Maximum employment as a pharmacy technician trainee
timing_deadlines.timeframe: 1500 hours or one year, whichever period is shorter
timing_deadlines.consequence: Work beyond the limit is unavailable unless the Board grants an extension, the individual has not yet reached 18, or the individual has not yet completed 500 trainee hours.

timing_deadlines.event: Application for a pharmacy technician licence after exceeding the trainee limits before turning 18
timing_deadlines.consequence: The application is the step the age exception was holding open, and the technician eligibility requirements still have to be satisfied.

timing_deadlines.event: Trainee hours supporting the examination route to licensure
timing_deadlines.timeframe: A minimum of 500 hours of employment as a pharmacy technician trainee
timing_deadlines.consequence: The hours are the alternative prerequisite to sitting the Board-approved assessment examination where no Board-approved training program has been completed.

timing_deadlines.event: Federal PREP Act coverage for qualified pharmacy technicians administering COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccines
timing_deadlines.consequence: The Declaration's coverage for these technician activities ends on that date as the Declaration now stands; the 247 CMR bar is unaffected either way.

forms_records.text: Documentation of the 500 trainee hours relied on for the examination route is attested to by the applicant under the pains and penalties of perjury and witnessed by the employer.

Written guidelines governing an on-the-job training program are formulated by the pharmacy consistently with professional, ethical and legal standards, and copies are provided to the Board on request.
A lapsed pharmacy technician licence is renewed by filing a renewal application with payment of an annual licence fee, applicable back fees and a late fee.
The title in use has to track the credential actually held, so an individual whose certification has lapsed uses the title pharmacy technician.

A written description of the duties delegated to certified pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technicians and pharmacy technician trainees, and of their scopes of responsibility, is made available to the Board on request under 247 CMR 8.06(1).

role_duties.duty: Work only within the duties of a pharmacy technician, only while acting under the direct supervision of a pharmacist, and never take prescriptions over the telephone.

Perform the technical work the pharmacy delegates under the pharmacist's direct supervision, relay the pharmacist's offer to counsel, seek the pharmacist on duty's approval before requesting refill authorizations, confirm that nothing has changed from the previous prescription, and refer anything requiring professional judgment to the pharmacist.

Identify him or herself as a certified pharmacy technician before speaking to the prescriber or the prescriber's agent, obtain the pharmacist on duty's approval before receiving new or omitted prescription information, taking a new prescription by telephone or performing a Schedule VI transfer, and stay clear of therapy clarification, drug utilization review, counseling and final dispensing process validation.

role_duties.role: Certified pharmacy technician whose certification has lapsed
role_duties.duty: Work within the duties and responsibilities of a pharmacy technician under 247 CMR 8.02, use the title pharmacy technician, and expect to be counted as a pharmacy technician in the supervisory ratios.

Give technicians and trainees direct supervision by overseeing and directing their activities, approve the specific technician communications the regulations condition on approval, and retain the judgmental functions, which 247 CMR does not allow to be delegated to any technician tier.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist Manager of Record, or Director of Pharmacy in an institutional pharmacy
role_duties.duty: Keep a list of the certified pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technicians and trainees employed, a written description of the duties delegated to them and a written description of their scopes of responsibility available to the Board on request.
Train a pharmacy technician or trainee under written pharmacy guidelines consistent with professional, ethical and legal standards, and produce copies of those guidelines to the Board on request.
Renew the licence on the two-year birthdate cycle and stop working once it has expired, since renewal restores the credential going forward rather than retroactively.

role_duties.role: Applicant for a pharmacy technician licence
role_duties.duty: Satisfy the four common requirements, choose one of the three alternatives, and prepare for all six knowledge areas the Board-approved assessment examination covers.

role_duties.role: Qualified pharmacy technician relying on the federal PREP Act Declaration
role_duties.duty: Meet every condition the Declaration sets, including State licensure or registration, supervision by a State-licensed pharmacist who is readily and immediately available, ACPE-approved practical training and a current basic CPR certificate, and act only for the vaccines, ages and period it names.

common_traps.text: Reading 247 CMR 8.02(6) as the complete list of what a technician may do. It sets a name-tag duty, two conditioned communications and the prohibited functions; ordinary technical work is delegated pharmacy work done under the pharmacist's direct supervision.
Treating direct supervision as a trainee-only condition. 247 CMR 2.00 defines the pharmacy technician, like the trainee, as performing pharmacy duties under the direct supervision of a pharmacist.
Reading the three eligibility alternatives as cumulative requirements. Certification is one route in, not a precondition to the others.
Treating the assessment examination as a standalone route, or treating completion of a training program as the licence itself rather than as the prerequisite to the examination.
Combining the 120-hour theoretical and 120-hour practical minimums into a single 240-hour total that any split can satisfy.
Reading the trainee limit as 1500 hours or one year, whichever is longer. The regulation takes the shorter period, and only three exceptions extend it.
Letting direct supervision cure the trainee telephone prohibition. The carve-out is written as an exception to the very grant that supervision unlocks.

Assuming the pharmacist's advance approval of a pharmacy technician's refill calls extends to whatever the call produces. Approval operates inside the unchanged-information condition of 247 CMR 8.02(6)(c), not around it.

Believing a written pharmacy protocol or the pharmacist's remote availability can convert a judgmental function into a technical task. Under 247 CMR the prohibited list is closed to both technician tiers however the pharmacy documents the workflow; the federal PREP Act coverage for certain vaccines rests on federal law and its own conditions, not on a pharmacy protocol.
Extending the certified technician's transfer authority beyond Schedule VI because the pharmacist has approved. Approval is a precondition to a narrow authority, not a way to widen it.
Stopping at scope and title when a certification lapses and missing the supervisory-ratio consequence, which is the one that can break a staffed shift.
Confusing a lapsed certification with a lapsed Board licence. The first narrows what the individual may do; the second makes any further work unlicensed practice.
Expecting a grace period on the technician licence, or expecting back fees and a late fee to make the interim shifts lawful in retrospect.

Assuming the technician examination is a calculations examination. Practice settings, the technician's duties in relationship to other pharmacy personnel, law and patient confidentiality are all named knowledge areas.

Reading the unchanged-information proviso into the certified technician's grant. 247 CMR 8.04(4)(c) does not repeat it and lets the certified technician, with approval, receive new or omitted prescription information; therapy clarification or modification stays closed.
Checking a training program's hours and forgetting its content. On the examination route 247 CMR 8.02(3)(e)3.a names the topics the program must cover.

Answering a technician vaccine question from one body of law. 247 CMR bars technician administration; the federal PREP Act Declaration covers qualified pharmacy technicians for COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccines on stated conditions through December 31, 2029.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 8.02(3) an applicant for a pharmacy technician license shall be at least 18 years old, a high school graduate or equivalent or currently enrolled in such a program, of good moral character, not convicted of a drug-related felony or having admitted to sufficient facts to warrant such a finding, and shall satisfy one of three alternatives: hold certification from a Board-approved certifying body; hold a substantially equivalent technician license in good standing in another state; or achieve a Board-approved passing score on a Board-approved assessment examination after completing either a Board-approved training program or a minimum of 500 hours of employment as a pharmacy technician trainee attested under the pains and penalties of perjury and witnessed by the employer.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 8.07(1) a pharmacy technician license expires every two years on the birthdate of the licensee. Under 247 CMR 8.07(2) any practice as a pharmacy technician after the expiration date constitutes unlicensed practice and subjects the individual to the penalties established for unlicensed practice. Under 247 CMR 8.07(3) a lapsed license may be renewed on filing a renewal application with the annual license fee, applicable back fees and a late fee, and under 247 CMR 8.07(4) a license lapsed more than two years may require other Board-determined conditions before renewal.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 8.02(5) a Board-approved pharmacy technician examination shall cover practice settings; the duties and responsibilities of a pharmacy technician in relationship to other pharmacy personnel; laws and regulations regarding the practice of pharmacy and patient confidentiality; medical abbreviations and symbols; common dosage calculations; and identification of drugs, dosages, routes of administration and storage requirements.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 8.02(4) a Board-approved training program may include a pharmacy technician training program accredited by the American Society of Health System Pharmacists; a program provided by a branch of the United States Armed Services or Public Health Service; a Board-approved program which includes a minimum of 120 hours of theoretical and 120 hours of practical instruction; or any other pharmacy technician training course approved by the Board. Under 247 CMR 8.06(2) a pharmacist may train a technician or trainee through an on-the-job training program complying with written pharmacy guidelines consistent with professional, ethical and legal standards, copies of which shall be provided to the Board on request.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 8.03(2) a pharmacy technician trainee must be at least 16 years of age, a high school graduate or equivalent or currently enrolled in such a program, of good moral character, and not convicted of a drug-related felony. Under 247 CMR 8.03(4)(b) and (c) a trainee may be authorized to perform the duties of a pharmacy technician under the direct supervision of a pharmacist but may not take prescriptions over the telephone. Under 247 CMR 8.03(5) an individual may not work as a trainee for more than 1500 hours or more than one year, whichever is shorter, unless the Board grants an extension, the individual has not yet reached 18 years of age, or the individual has not yet completed at least 500 hours as a trainee; an individual who worked beyond those limits before turning 18 shall apply for a pharmacy technician license within 30 days of the 18th birthday.

individual has not yet completed 500 hours as a trainee

authority.name: Massachusetts pharmacy technician scope and pharmacist responsibility

exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 8.04(4)(c) a certified pharmacy technician, after identifying him or herself as such, may request refill authorizations from the prescriber or the prescriber's agent and, with the approval of the pharmacist on duty, receive new or omitted prescription information, including communicating information recorded on a patient profile that does not require professional judgment or interpretation. Under 247 CMR 8.04(4)(e) a certified pharmacy technician may not administer medications or vaccines, perform drug utilization review, conduct clinical conflict resolution, contact prescribers about therapy clarification or modification, provide patient counseling, or perform final dispensing process validation.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 2.00 a Pharmacy Technician is an individual who is registered by the Board, pursuant to 247 CMR 8.02, who performs pharmacy duties under the direct supervision of a pharmacist; a Pharmacy Technician Trainee is an individual preparing to be registered as a pharmacy technician who performs pharmacy duties under the direct supervision of a pharmacist; and a Certified Pharmacy Technician is a pharmacy technician who is currently registered by the Board and certified by a Board-approved certifying body. Under 247 CMR 8.04(1) and (2), no individual may work as a certified pharmacy technician without holding a valid pharmacy technician license from the Board, and a certified pharmacy technician means a pharmacy technician that is certified by a Board-approved certifying body.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 8.06(1) a pharmacist Manager of Record, or the Director of Pharmacy in an institutional pharmacy, that uses certified pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technicians or pharmacy technician trainees shall make available to the Board on request a list of currently employed such personnel, a written description of the duties delegated to them, and a written description of their scopes of responsibility. authority.name: Declaration Under the Public Readiness and Emergency Preparedness Act for Medical Countermeasures Against COVID-19, 12th Amendment, 89 FR 99875 (Dec. 11, 2024)
authority.section: Declaration sections V(d), V(i) and XII(i) as republished, and the Supplementary Information statement on preemption

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The Declaration Under the Public Readiness and Emergency Preparedness Act for Medical Countermeasures Against COVID-19, as amended and republished in full by its 12th Amendment (89 FR 99875, December 11, 2024, effective January 1, 2025), identifies in section V(d) as qualified persons the pharmacy interns and qualified pharmacy technicians who administer, if the intern or technician acts under the supervision of a State-licensed pharmacist and is licensed or registered by his or her State board of pharmacy, (1) vaccines that CDC/ACIP recommend to persons ages three through 18 according to CDC's/ACIP's standard immunization schedule, (2) seasonal influenza vaccine that CDC/ACIP recommends to persons aged 19 and older according to that schedule, or (3) FDA-authorized or FDA-licensed COVID-19 vaccines to persons ages three or older. They are qualified persons only if the listed requirements are met, including that the vaccine is authorized, approved, or licensed by the FDA; a COVID-19 vaccination is ordered and administered according to CDC's/ACIP's COVID-19 vaccine recommendations, and a childhood vaccination or a technician-administered seasonal influenza vaccination according to CDC's/ACIP's standard immunization schedule; the supervising pharmacist is readily and immediately available to the immunizing qualified pharmacy technician; the technician has completed a practical training program approved by the ACPE that includes hands-on injection technique, clinical evaluation of indications and contraindications of vaccines, and the recognition and treatment of emergency reactions to vaccines; the technician has a current certificate in basic cardiopulmonary resuscitation; and the technician complies with any applicable requirements (or conditions of use) set forth in the CDC COVID-19 vaccination provider agreement and any other federal requirements that apply to the administration of COVID-19 vaccines. Under section XII(i), liability protections for qualified pharmacy technicians who administer COVID-19 vaccines to individuals aged three and above, CDC/ACIP recommended seasonal influenza vaccines to persons aged three through 18, and seasonal influenza vaccines to individuals aged nineteen and above last through December 31, 2029; other vaccines recommended for persons aged three through 18 are covered for the periods set by other paragraphs of section XII. The amendment states that, to the extent any State law would otherwise prohibit these qualified persons from prescribing, dispensing, or administering Covered Countermeasures that are COVID-19 vaccines, seasonal influenza vaccines or COVID-19 tests, such law is preempted. Sections V(i) and XII(i) separately cover qualified pharmacy technicians who, under the supervision of a State-licensed pharmacist, administer FDA-authorized, approved, or licensed COVID-19 therapeutics subcutaneously, intramuscularly, or orally, on conditions that include a supervising pharmacist readily and immediately available, ACPE-approved practical training for injected therapeutics and a current certificate in basic cardiopulmonary resuscitation; for the therapeutics identified in section VII(d) of the Declaration that coverage lasts through December 31, 2029.
exceptions: Coverage depends on every listed condition, including supervision by a State-licensed pharmacist who is readily and immediately available, ACPE-approved practical training and a current basic cardiopulmonary resuscitation certificate.
The stated coverage for technician-administered COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccines ends on December 31, 2029.

full_prose_under_review.title: Massachusetts Pharmacy Support Personnel: Supervisory Ratios, Identification and Schedule II Handling
full_prose_under_review.subtopic: Who is counted in the supervisory ratios of 247 CMR 8.06(3) and how credential composition unlocks them, the name tag and title each tier must display under 247 CMR 8.01(14), 8.02(6)(a), 8.03(4)(a) and 8.04(4)(a), the transporting-versus-handling line for Schedule II stock in 247 CMR 8.05, and the Manager of Record's production duties under 247 CMR 8.06(1) and (2) and absence duties under 247 CMR 9.23(5)
learning_objectives: Identify which staff fall inside the supervisory ratio in 247 CMR 8.06(3)(a) and which 247 CMR 8.06(3)(b) removes from it, and state the two conditions that exclusion carries.
Test a proposed roster against the three composition conditions that unlock a four-person ratio and the single condition attached to a three-person ratio.
State what each of the four tiers must display on a name tag, and identify the one provision that does not confine the tag to a first name.
Separate assisting in the transporting of Schedule II controlled substances from assisting in the handling of them, and attach each to the correct technician grade.
State the conditions in 247 CMR 8.05(2) on which both Schedule II grants depend, and explain why satisfying them does not enlarge the narrower grant.
Apply the hydrocodone-only extended release prohibition in 247 CMR 8.05(3) by product rather than by credential, and name the category the provision expressly permits.
List the three document sets a Manager of Record must make available to the Board on request under 247 CMR 8.06(1), and identify the tier those documents do not cover.
Place a planned and an unplanned Manager of Record absence on the 30-day, five-day and 100-day thresholds in 247 CMR 9.23(5), and say who performs the controlled substances inventory in each case.

orientation.text: Massachusetts sizes a pharmacy's support staff by composition rather than by headcount, so the first move in any ratio question is to decide who is in the count at all. 247 CMR 8.06(3)(a) addresses a pharmacist utilizing pharmacy interns, certified pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technicians, and pharmacy technician trainees to assist in filling prescriptions, so the count starts with the members of those four categories whom the pharmacist is actually using for that work. 247 CMR 8.06(3)(b) then provides that sales clerks, messengers, delivery personnel, secretaries and any other persons who do not fall within those four definitions shall not be included, but only as long as such persons are not supporting the pharmacist in any professional capacity. The exclusion therefore has two limbs. The first asks whether the person falls within one of the four definitions, and those definitions are not bare titles: 247 CMR 2.00 describes the pharmacy technician and the pharmacy technician trainee as individuals who perform pharmacy duties under the direct supervision of a pharmacist. The second asks what the person is actually doing, and a front-store employee drawn into prescription work during a rush fails it at the moment the work changes and is counted from then on. The same logic reaches a licensed technician assigned only to the register: the ratio counts support personnel the pharmacist is utilizing to assist in filling prescriptions, so the licence alone does not put that employee in the count, and prescription work does. Nothing in the provision keys the count to the job title printed on a schedule.

The ratios themselves are two, and each carries its own composition condition. Under 247 CMR 8.06(3)(a)1 one pharmacist may supervise a maximum of four support personnel, provided at least one of the four support personnel is a certified pharmacy technician and one is a pharmacy intern; or at least two of the support personnel are certified pharmacy technicians; or two of the support personnel are pharmacy interns. Under 247 CMR 8.06(3)(a)2 one pharmacist may supervise a maximum of three support personnel, provided at least one of the three is a pharmacy intern or a certified pharmacy technician. The three routes to four are alternatives, and each names a credential twice over: the first pairs one certified pharmacy technician with one pharmacy intern, the second asks for two certified pharmacy technicians, and the third asks for two pharmacy interns. A pharmacy technician trainee satisfies none of them, and neither does a pharmacy technician, however current the licence. Both ratios are stated as conditions on a maximum, so a roster satisfying no condition does not fall back to a larger number; it falls out of the ratio it was trying to claim.

Identification is what makes that composition visible from the other side of the counter, and 247 CMR 8.00 states it four times, once for each tier. Under 247 CMR 8.01(14) a pharmacy intern shall wear a name tag which indicates the intern's name and the words pharmacy intern. Under 247 CMR 8.02(6)(a) a pharmacy technician shall wear a name tag which indicates the individual's first name and the title Pharmacy Technician. Under 247 CMR 8.03(4)(a) a pharmacy technician trainee shall wear a name tag with the individual's first name and the title Pharmacy Technician Trainee, and under 247 CMR 8.04(4)(a) a certified pharmacy technician shall wear a name tag with the individual's first name and the title Certified Pharmacy Technician. The three technician provisions are drafted in matching terms and confine the tag to the individual's first name; the intern provision is the one that asks instead for the intern's name. In every case the title stated is the title of a credential rather than a description of the work being done that shift, so the tag follows the credential the individual actually holds and not what the pharmacy has assigned. For the certified tier that credential is not a separate Board licence: under 247 CMR 8.04(1) and (2) and the 247 CMR 2.00 definition, a certified pharmacy technician is a pharmacy technician holding the Board's pharmacy technician licence who is currently certified by a Board-approved certifying body. A current certified pharmacy technician therefore wears the 247 CMR 8.04(4)(a) tag, and under 247 CMR 8.04(3) one whose certification has lapsed must use the title pharmacy technician.

Schedule II stock is governed by 247 CMR 8.05, and the section opens by refusing to move the thing that matters: under 247 CMR 8.05(1) accountability for and security of Schedule II controlled substances shall be the direct responsibility of the pharmacist. What 247 CMR 8.05(2) then permits, under the supervision of a pharmacist, is assistance, and it is sized differently for the two technician grades. A pharmacy technician may assist in the transporting of Schedule II controlled substances. A certified pharmacy technician may assist in the transporting and handling of them. Both grants sit behind one proviso: the pharmacist must have approved the certified pharmacy technician or pharmacy technician to assist in the handling or transporting of Schedule II controlled substances, and that approval must be evidenced by written policies and procedures to be followed in the pharmacy, which shall be made available to the Board on request. The proviso is a condition on each grant rather than a way to enlarge either, so approving a pharmacy technician in writing does not convert a transporting grant into the certified technician's transporting and handling grant. What passes to either grade is assistance with the physical movement or handling of the stock, and not the pharmacist's professional judgment.

Two features of 247 CMR 8.05 are easy to state backwards. The first is where pharmacy interns sit. The section is titled as requirements for the handling of Schedule II controlled substances by pharmacy interns, certified pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technicians, and pharmacy technician trainees, but the operative grants in 247 CMR 8.05(2) name the pharmacy technician and the certified pharmacy technician, and the one express permission the section gives a pharmacy intern is in 247 CMR 8.05(3). The second is the shape of that subsection. It provides that a certified pharmacy technician, pharmacy technician, or pharmacy technician trainee may not handle any hydrocodone-only extended release medication that is not in an abuse deterrent form, and that pharmacy interns under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist may handle it. The prohibition is drawn by product and names all three technician grades at once, so climbing the credential ladder does not escape it and the pharmacist's approval under 247 CMR 8.05(2) does not reach it. What does take a product outside the prohibition is the formulation, because an abuse deterrent hydrocodone-only extended release product is not what 247 CMR 8.05(3) describes.

The duties owed by the person running the pharmacy are stated in 247 CMR 8.06(1) and (2), and they are duties of production rather than of filing. A pharmacist Manager of Record, or the Director of Pharmacy in an institutional pharmacy, which utilizes certified pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technicians, or pharmacy technician trainees shall make three things available to the Board upon request: a list of currently employed certified pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technicians and pharmacy technician trainees; a written description of the duties delegated to them; and a written description of their scopes of responsibility. Nothing is lodged with the Board in advance, so never having filed the documents is not the shape of the duty and is no answer to an inspector who asks for them. Note also which tier is absent from all three items: pharmacy interns are counted in the supervisory ratios under 247 CMR 8.06(3) but they are named neither in the 247 CMR 8.06(1) list nor in the delegated duties description nor in the scopes of responsibility description. Separately, 247 CMR 8.06(2) requires that on-the-job training programs comply with written guidelines formulated by the pharmacy in a manner consistent with professional, ethical, and legal standards of proper pharmacy practice, with copies of those guidelines provided to the Board on request.

Because the production duty in 247 CMR 8.06(1) attaches to a position rather than to an individual, what happens when that position empties is a support personnel question as much as a management one. 247 CMR 9.23(5) governs the temporary absence of a Manager of Record and turns on three numbers. A pharmacy shall appoint an Interim Manager who is registered by the Board prior to any planned absence of the Manager of Record that is expected to last 30 days or longer, and within five days of any unplanned absence that is likely to last 30 days or longer; the five-day allowance belongs to the unplanned branch, and reading it onto a planned leave is the standard error. Prior to the absence the Manager of Record shall perform a controlled substances inventory that is signed by the Manager of Record and the Interim Manager, and where the Manager of Record is unexpectedly not available another registered pharmacist shall perform that inventory, so the inventory duty changes hands rather than lapsing. The third number is the outer limit: where a Manager of Record is away from the position for 100 days or more, the pharmacy shall submit an application for a change of Manager of Record.
